dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agency personnel at the EPA and other relevant agencies involved in strategy development and reporting.
dimensions.evidence: The Administrator shall, in consultation with the heads of other Federal agencies... develop and carry out a National Critical Mineral Recovery Strategy

dimensions.assessment: Effects are primarily administrative, requiring interagency planning, identification of barriers, and periodic reports to Congress.
dimensions.evidence: transmit to the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives... a report that contains the Strategy

dimensions.assessment: The source material does not state or imply any specific federal spending authorization or direct revenue changes.
Amends the Solid Waste Disposal Act to create a new section 2009 for the National Critical Mineral Recovery Strategy.
dimensions.evidence: Subtitle B of the Solid Waste Disposal Act (42 U.S.C. 6911 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following new section

dimensions.assessment: Establishes an ongoing, permanent statutory requirement for strategies and biennial reporting to congressional committees.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this section, and every 2 years thereafter

missing_information: Specific funding levels or appropriations authorized to carry out the strategy.
Quantitative estimates of critical minerals expected to be recovered.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes a coordinating strategy within the EPA for critical mineral recovery and requires biennial reports to Congress, directing administrative actions and interagency consultation without imposing large-scale economic mandates or spending changes.
